properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: The secp256k1 curve the whole FEVM toolchain signs with: ethers v6 (package.json direct dep ^6.13.2) reaches @noble/curves for ECDSA transaction signing — the app's deployer account in hardhat.config.ts (process.env.PRIVATE_KEY → accounts) signs every deployment via this curve. Changeable here only via lockfile pin; the EVM's secp256k1 account system itself is fixed by the Filecoin/FEVM protocol. properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Available in the shipped library; no direct call site found in the application source (this kit signs with secp256k1 only — verified by grep of all non-lockfile files). Reachable at runtime through the installed ethers v6 stack. Changeable here via lockfile pin.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: elliptic 6.5.4 is the ECDSA backend of the ethers v5 half of the tree, pulled by @glif/filecoin-address@2.0.43 (yarn.lock:492-501) and hardhat plugins. The app's own signing goes through ethers v6/@noble instead. Changeable here via lockfile pin.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: @noble/curves@1.2.0 at yarn.lock:533 — one of three @noble/curves resolutions (also 1.4.2 and ~1.8.1). Provides P-256 ECDSA/ECDH primitives. In this kit, ethers v6 (the declared web3 library) uses @noble/curves for secp256k1 transaction signing; P-256 is part of the library's shipped surface. Observable here, replaceable only via upstream ethers migration to PQ signatures.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: elliptic@6.5.4 (yarn.lock:2518, plus a second resolution range at 2531). Classic ECC library used by older ethers/secp256k1 tooling — the ECDH implementation is part of its shipped surface. The application itself does not call ECDH directly; presence in the shipped dependency tree is what this entry records.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Deep transitive dependency of SSH-key tooling (sshpk/http-signature); no application call site — this project performs no key agreement. Observable here, changeable only via lockfile regeneration.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Password KDF for ethers v5 keystore files — quantum-safe, no Shor exposure. Available in the shipped tree; no direct app call site (the app's only key material is the env-sourced deployer key, handled by ethers v6). Changeable here via lockfile pin.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: @noble/hashes@1.2.0 at yarn.lock:554 (also resolved at 1.3.2/1.4.0/1.7.2). ethers v6 hashes transactions and messages with keccak256/sha256 from @noble/hashes — SHA-256 here is part of the library surface the build ships; the app's own .sol code uses Solidity keccak256 instead.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: PQ-safe hash available in the shipped library; no direct call site in the app (the app hashes on-chain via the Solidity keccak256 opcode, reported separately). Multiple @noble/hashes versions coexist in the lock (1.2.0, 1.3.2, 1.4.0, 1.7.2). Changeable here via lockfile pin.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: scrypt-js@2.0.4 at yarn.lock:5496 (a second resolution scrypt-js@3.0.1 at 5501 serves other requesters). scrypt is the password-based KDF ethers uses for JSON keystore files (Wallet.fromEncryptedJson); this kit manages dev-deployer keys via Hardhat network signers instead. scrypt is itself a memory-hard KDF with no Shor-relevant weakness — inventory entry for completeness.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: PQ-safe hash family. The application's own Keccak-256 use is the Solidity keccak256() in contracts/basic-deal-client/DealClient.sol:137 (reported as a separate finding); this object covers the JS-side SHA-3 implementation shipped in node_modules via ethers v6's noble stack. Changeable here via lockfile pin.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Symmetric authenticated encryption from tweetnacl's secretbox — not Shor-relevant (A+ rated). No application call site; available in the shipped tree via the sshpk chain. Observable here, changeable only via lockfile regeneration.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: tweetnacl@0.14.5 at yarn.lock:6226 (range "tweetnacl@^0.14.3, tweetnacl@~0.14.0"). Ships XSalsa20-Poly1305 AE, Ed25519 signatures and X25519 ECDH (all quantum-vulnerable primitives) — the deterministic scan already carries those as separate ALG objects. No call site in this repo's own source; presence in the shipped toolchain is what this records. tweetnacl 0.14.5 is also unmaintained (last release 2016).

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: scrypt is the memory-hard KDF ethers uses for keystore wallet encryption — PQ-safe. Two scrypt-js versions are pinned in the lock (2.0.4 and 3.0.1 at yarn.lock:287); both ship in the build. No direct app call site; the app's deployer key is env-sourced, never keystore-encrypted. Changeable here via lockfile pin.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: sha.js at yarn.lock:5617 (ranges ^2.4.0 and ^2.4.8). Streaming SHA-1/SHA-2 implementations shipped in the build; used by crypto-browserify-style polyfills in the hardhat toolchain. No direct call site in this repo's own source.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: The ECDSA/curve library of the ethers v5 half of the dependency tree (pulled by @glif/filecoin-address and hardhat plugins). The application signs via ethers v6/@noble, so elliptic is present-but-uncalled here; it still ships in the installed tree and any ethers v5 path (e.g. @glif's own address tooling) reaches it. Changeable here via lockfile pin.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: The hash library beneath ethers v6 (used for keccak256/sha256/ripemd160 across the noble stack). Multiple versions are pinned (1.2.0 under @noble/curves@1.2.0 at yarn.lock:538; also 1.3.2, 1.4.0, 1.7.2). Shipped in the build; no direct app call site — app hashing goes through ethers or the EVM keccak256 opcode. Changeable here via lockfile pin.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: The ethers v5 hash backend (SHA-256/RIPEMD-160 for @ethersproject/sha2/signing-key). Shipped in the build; the app's own hash uses are the Solidity keccak256 opcode and @glif's blakejs checksum, both reported separately. Changeable here via lockfile pin.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: @noble/curves@1.2.0 at yarn.lock:533 — the library object for the same resolution as ALG-a6da3577 (P-256 via @noble/curves@1.2.0). Three @noble/curves versions resolve (1.2.0, 1.4.2, ~1.8.1); the library ships secp256k1, P-256, Ed25519, X25519 and more — the secp256k1 surface is what ethers v6 uses for every transaction this Hardhat kit signs.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Node PBKDF2 wrapper beneath @ethersproject/pbkdf2 — quantum-safe password KDF for ethers v5 keystore files. Shipped in the build, no direct app call site. Changeable here via lockfile pin.
